mechanism: Alcohol may potentiate gastrointestinal side effects of cefuroxime and theoretical disulfiram-like reaction is possible with some cephalosporins containing methyltetrazole side chain (not present in cefuroxime), but cefuroxime itself has minimal hepatic metabolism and does not significantly inhibit aldehyde dehydrogenase.
action: Counsel patients to limit alcohol consumption during cefuroxime therapy to minimize gastrointestinal upset; no absolute contraindication exists but caution is warranted.
